title: 'Bitter' Roy Keane claps back at Erling Haaland's dad - 'You’re seeing the game differently' | talkSPORT
text:
Haaland Sr. sarcastically congratulated referee Clement Turpin and Jude Bellingham after his country crashed out of the World Cup.

The former Manchester City and Leeds United player went viral several times while watching from the stands at Miami Stadium.

The 53-year-old visibly accused Djed Spence of diving with an exaggerated hand gesture after the Tottenham defender thought he had won a penalty for England in extra time, before the decision was overturned by VAR.

He was then caught seconds later flicking his two fingers up in the air and appearing to mouth the words: "F*** off."

The retired 31-cap Norwegian international then claimed his son and his teammates were robbed in a jab at the officials post-match.

In reply to a post on X regarding Bellingham's second goal against Norway to put England into the lead in extra time, Haaland wrote: "Well done Bellingham and referee."

He later added: "Really? Saved by the referee. Hope you win the WC now. But feel we got robbed today."

Ian Wright, however, insisted Norway only had themselves to blame while reacting to Alfie Haaland’s remarks on Stick to Football.

England had a higher xG than Norway, more shots on target and in total, more touches in the opposition box and more possession.

"Is that sour grapes from Alf-Inge Haaland, saying well done to Bellingham and the referee?" Arsenal legend Wright asked.

"I think that was just a bit of a low blow from him."

On Torbjørn Heggem disallowed goal for a Haaland foul on Elliot Anderson, Wright continued: "He can’t surely be referring to that because that was just a ridiculous push [from Haaland].

"In that particular moment, he’s like six or seven inches taller; why does he need to be that aggressive with him?

"It’s a massive foul. You can’t be talking that."

Manchester United legend Keane admitted that Norway could feel slightly aggrieved by the refereeing, but nothing that would amount to what Haaland Sr could claim as a 'robbery'.

"I think the referee was giving England a lot of calls, 50-50s. I’m not talking about the major ones," Keane said.

"He seemed to be just on the side of England, which can happen in a game.

"I’m not sitting here going, 'He’s cost Norway', absolutely not. But there was calls when you’re going… it could have gone the other way."

He later joked: "Will he remember the game? Because he always seems to be drinking alcohol at the matches, the dad.

"No, he does! If you’re having a drink then you’re seeing the game differently.

"Listen, I’ll always be trying to go the other way [against England] a little bit, if it’s 50-50, but the push is a push, and then he heads it, so there you go.

"Families and fans after games, we saw the interviews with the England manager, Bellingham, family members, they’re all a bit emotional so you try and give them the benefit of the doubt.

"But when people wake up tomorrow morning, you won’t be sitting there going, 'The referee’s cost us', you can’t.

"You can argue a couple of decisions, but you can’t say, 'He’s cost us', no."

Former Aston Villa star Gabby Agbonlahor had a brutal response to Keane on World Cup Breakfast.

Agbonlahor, who was at Villa when Keane was assistant manager, said:  “Roy's a bitter guy though, like I said before, I had him at Villa. But at least Haaland hasn't walked out of his country at a World Cup.”

When asked whether grown me should be behaving like Haaland did, Agbonlahor added: “But I feel like it's going to be like that for Haaland's dad, he's devastated his son's not scored and his country's going home.”
